lens.subject: Does one bundle per run replace per-skill sends in the delivery doc?
lens.message:
The memory you saved settles where reaction delivery belongs. You put it this way: "we route every reaction through one bundle per run per person, not one message per skill — a person should get one thing to read, not four." You also held the batching window against Tina's pushback: the bundle closes when the run closes, and a skill that misses the close waits for the next run. Per-skill delivery with client-side collapsing was considered and rejected because it moves the ordering problem onto the reader.

[The reaction delivery doc](docs/reaction-delivery.md) says the opposite of the ruling. Its opening reads: "Each reaction skill sends its own message to the person as soon as it finishes: the refraction, the question and the review each arrive on their own, in whatever order the skills complete. Readers collapse duplicates on their side." That is the rejected alternative, written as current policy. After the change it would say every reaction routes through one bundle per run per person, closed when the run closes, with late skills waiting for the next run — resting on your ruling rather than on reader-side collapsing.

Is that the right way to read what moved: one bundle per run is now the rule, and per-skill sends are off the table? If I have it wrong, tell me how.

This is the only document in the repo it reaches; nothing else describes how reactions are sent.
